note: Second opinion on source-probe-10. Its probe of the majority page is confirmed by my own re-probe, but its conclusion -- 'a stale curated name for CURATION.md, not a URL that has yet to be found ... no other URL helps' -- is wrong on the second half, and I found the page it missed. https://democrats-waysandmeans.house.gov/subcommittees/select-revenue-measures-118th-congress is a readable .gov page (869 readable characters, above the verifier's 400-character floor) and the probe's verdict for this node is 'labelled': it carries 'Select Revenue Measures (118th Congress)' as its title and again as a breadcrumb heading and twice more in its hearing listings, all in the content region, matching under rule committee_scaffolding_folded once canonical_name_key drops the parenthetical. Its index, https://democrats-waysandmeans.house.gov/subcommittees/, labels it too but serves only 238 readable characters, so the verifier would record nothing from that one. I deliberately did NOT nominate either URL, and the owner should decide rather than me: this node already publishes verificationFailure 'not_in_official_list' from the House Clerk's complete committee list (listedNames: Health, Oversight, Social Security, Tax, Trade, Work and Welfare), and data_pipeline/verification/directories.py skips the not_in_official_list stamp on any node that already carries a sourceUrl. A confirmation off a page whose own title says '(118th Congress)' would therefore silently replace a strong, current, complete-list negative with 'its official page names it', dated the day of the fetch. That trades a true negative for an archival positive and reads as if the subcommittee were current. The substantive finding for CURATION.md is unchanged and now better evidenced: this is the 118th Congress's subcommittee, the committee's own minority site files it under that Congress, and the majority renamed the jurisdiction 'Tax'.

note: Second opinion on source-probe-10. Its reading of the majority page is right and I reproduced it, but its conclusion -- 'A rename to the committee's current wording, argued in CURATION.md, is the fix; no other URL helps' -- is wrong on both halves. (1) Another URL does name it: https://democrats-waysandmeans.house.gov/ , the committee Democrats' current official site, serves 51,563 bytes of HTML reducing to 1,122 readable characters (above the 400-character floor) and the probe's verdict for this node is 'labelled', matched text 'Worker & Family Support', region content, rule committee_scaffolding_folded. The label sits in that page's own subcommittee list, which reads Health, Oversight, Social Security, Tax, Trade, Worker & Family Support -- six entries, with NO Congress qualifier, i.e. the minority side of this committee still uses the curated name today for the body the House Clerk calls 'Work and Welfare'. A dedicated page exists too: https://democrats-waysandmeans.house.gov/subcommittees/worker-family-support-118th-congress , 783 readable characters, verdict 'labelled' as 'Worker & Family Support (118th Congress)'. (2) So this is not simply a stale name. Renaming the node to the majority's 'Work & Welfare' would settle a live disagreement between two official House sources by fiat, and CURATION.md should record the disagreement rather than pick a side. I deliberately did NOT nominate either URL: this node publishes verificationFailure 'not_in_official_list' from the House Clerk's complete list, and data_pipeline/verification/directories.py drops that stamp for any node that acquires a sourceUrl, so a confirmation here would replace 'the Clerk's list carries no unit of this name, it carries Work and Welfare' with 'its official page names it'. The Clerk badge, which prints the list's own six names beside the failure, tells a reader more than the confirmation would. Owner's call, not mine; both URLs are written down here so it costs one line to make.
